evidence: migration duration 2ms, longest transaction 0ms
writer max stall 2ms (threshold 50ms)
query plan unchanged, 0 rows seq-scanned before and after

review.summary: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on orders.status is safe to run as-is.
evidence: max writer stall 2ms (threshold 50ms)
longest transaction 279ms (threshold 2000ms)
affected query plan unchanged, 0 rows seq-scanned before and after

review.summary: Adding the FK as NOT VALID then validating separately avoids blocking writers and stays well under all hazard thresholds.
evidence: max writer stall 2ms (threshold 50ms)
longest transaction 81ms (threshold 2000ms)
constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table=false, query plans unchanged (0 rows seq-scanned before/after)
review.action: Ship the migration as written; no changes needed.

review.summary: Adding a NOT NULL column with a volatile DEFAULT clock_timestamp() forces a full-table rewrite under AccessExclusiveLock, stalling concurrent writers for ~500ms.
evidence: Original migration: concurrent writer max_stall_ms=496 (threshold 50ms), locks_held include orders: AccessExclusiveLock
Original migration longest_transaction_ms=500 while rewriting 1M rows
Fixed migration: max_stall_ms=43, longest_transaction_ms=94, schema_equivalent=true
review.action: Replace the single ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp() with the batched nullable-add + backfill + NOT VALID/VALIDATE/SET NOT NULL sequence provided.

review.summary: ALTER COLUMN TYPE bigint rewrites the whole orders table under AccessExclusiveLock, stalling concurrent writers for 470ms — use the add-column/backfill/swap pattern instead.
evidence: Concurrent writer max_stall_ms=470 (threshold 50ms) during original migration
Migration held AccessExclusiveLock on orders for a 467ms transaction while rewriting 1M rows
Fixed version reduced max writer stall to 4ms and longest transaction to 102ms with identical resulting schema
review.action: Replace the direct ALTER COLUMN TYPE with the add-column/backfill/trigger-swap migration before deploying to production.

review.summary: CREATE INDEX (non-concurrent) on orders takes a ShareLock and stalls the concurrent writer for 197ms, exceeding the 50ms threshold; use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY instead.
evidence: Original migration: writer max_stall_ms=197 with ShareLock held on orders
Fixed migration (CONCURRENTLY): writer max_stall_ms=2 with ShareUpdateExclusiveLock only
verify_fix confirms schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_idx ON orders (status);
review.action: Replace the migration with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (run outside a transaction block) to avoid blocking writers.

review.summary: The single-statement UPDATE backfilling 1M rows runs as one 3.5s transaction that stalls concurrent writers for 3.2s; batch it instead.
evidence: Original migration: longest_transaction_ms=3487, writer max_stall_ms=3175 (threshold 2000ms/50ms)
Batched fix: longest_transaction_ms=94, writer max_stall_ms=2
verify_fix reports schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true
review.action: Replace the single UPDATE with the batched DO-block backfill (COMMIT per 20k-row range) before deploying.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN notes irreversibly destroys the notes data for all 1,000,000 rows (including the ~10% with non-null values) even though it runs fast and lock-free, so per policy it must be classified DATA_LOSS regardless of timing.
evidence: simulate_migration confirms dropped_columns: ["orders.notes"] with duration 3ms and writer stall 8ms (well under thresholds) — fast but the drop itself is irrecoverable
~10% of 1,000,000 seeded orders rows have non-null notes ('gift wrap'), all destroyed with no backup

verify_fix of a rename-to-deprecate alternative produced schema_equivalent:false (extra column notes_deprecated), proving no schema-preserving rewrite exists that reaches the exact same end state without permanently removing the data — the requested end state itself is the data-loss event
review.action: Do not run the DROP COLUMN as a single silent migration; first rename the column to notes_deprecated (and optionally back up its non-null values) for a deprecation window, then drop it in a follow-up migration once stakeholders confirm the data is truly unused.

review.summary: Narrowing customers.email to varchar(20) silently truncates over 10,000 existing rows (max length 21, but ~10001 rows exceed 20 chars), corrupting unique email data.
evidence: simulate_migration reported lossy_changes: customers.email longest existing value 21 chars truncated to varchar(20)
Guard-check fix found 10001 of 20000 rows (50%) exceed 20 chars, far more than a single outlier
Migration itself completes in 40ms with only 7ms writer stall, so timing is fine — the hazard is purely silent truncation of data
review.action: Block this migration until the ~10,000 customer rows with emails longer than 20 characters are identified and handled explicitly (re-verify/contact affected users or raise the UI limit) instead of silently truncating their email addresses.

review.summary: Adding the FK constraint validates it inline against all 1M existing orders rows, stalling concurrent writers for 83ms and holding a ShareRowExclusiveLock during the scan.
evidence: constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table: true, writer max_stall_ms 83 (>50ms threshold)
Original migration takes ShareRowExclusiveLock on orders vs ShareUpdateExclusiveLock in fix
Fix reduces writer stall to 9ms and keeps schema_equivalent:true with clean_under_thresholds:true
review.fixed_migration:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2 FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2;
review.action: Apply the FK as NOT VALID first, then run VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate statement to avoid blocking writers during the validation scan.

review.summary: Dropping orders_customer_id_idx is not actually unused: it forces recent_orders_for_customer.sql into a full sequential scan of all 1M rows instead of an index scan.
evidence: Post-migration plan shows Seq Scan reading 1,000,002 rows vs 0 before (threshold 100,000)
Query execution time rose from 0.037ms to 13.3ms, a ~359x slowdown (threshold 5x)
Fix verified: adding covering index (customer_id, created_at DESC) then dropping old index CONCURRENTLY keeps writer stall at 7ms and returns query to Index Scan at 0.016ms
review.fixed_migration:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_created_at_idx ON orders (customer_id, created_at DESC);
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_idx;
review.action: Replace the plain DROP INDEX with the verified fix: create a concurrent covering index on (customer_id, created_at DESC) first, then drop the old index concurrently, before merging.

review.summary: The migration creates an index on raw `status`, but the weekly_paid_report query filters on `lower(status)`, so the index is never used and the query still seq-scans all 2,000,001 rows.
evidence: weekly_paid_report seq-scanned 2,000,001 rows both before (107.1ms) and after (113.0ms) the migration
fixed migration (expression index on lower(status), created_at) cut execution to 8.6ms with 0 rows seq-scanned
writer stall stayed at 2ms in both original and fixed versions, so locking was never the issue
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_lower_created_at_idx ON orders (lower(status), created_at);
review.action: Replace the migration with an expression index on (lower(status), created_at) so the weekly_paid_report query can actually use it.

review.summary: Adding orders.first_seen_at NOT NULL DEFAULT now() is metadata-only in modern Postgres and safe to run as-is.

review.summary: Narrowing customers.email to varchar(40) is safe since all existing emails fit and the migration runs a quick metadata-only rewrite with negligible writer impact.

Longest transaction 10ms (<2000ms threshold)
No dropped columns/tables, no lossy changes, row counts unchanged (20000 customers, 1M orders)
review.action: Proceed with the migration as written; no changes needed.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN notes SET NOT NULL fails outright because ~10% of the 1M seeded rows already have NULL notes.
evidence: simulate_migration errored: "column \"notes\" of relation \"orders\" contains null values"
Fixed version: longest_transaction_ms=92 (batched backfill), max writer stall 2ms, 0 lock_timeout_errors
verify_fix reports clean_under_thresholds: true, schema_equivalent: true
review.action: Backfill existing NULL notes in small batched transactions (e.g. to empty string or a sentinel), validate a NOT VALID check constraint, then apply SET NOT NULL, instead of running the bare ALTER on the populated table.
